messages:
InfraBot: :rotating_light: Incident detected: GPU queue depth exceeded threshold in eu-west-1 pool. Alerts: queue_length=980, avg_wait_ms=3450, active_gpus=48/60, autoscaler_attempts=6, autoscaler_failures=4. Paginated to #incidents and paging oncall.
Asha (oncall): acknowledged — looking now. Which pools exactly?
Samir: eu-west-1/gpu-pool-7 and gpu-pool-8. Pool 8 shows node flaps and repeated CUDA Xid errors in kernel logs.
Ben: I can pull driver logs, give me ~2m.
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Incident IN-9923 triggered, urgency: high — Asha (oncall) assigned.
Asha (oncall): copying initial mitigation steps: 1) stop scheduling new jobs to pool-8, 2) route suspect customer traffic to fallback pool, 3) try graceful drain of flapping nodes.
Lena: routing rule: setting model-route weight for "prod/completions" to eu-west-1/pool-5 (lower-capacity but stable) — doing a 50% shift now.
Samir: pool-8 nodes—I see repeated messages: 
```
[2026-03-15T02:10:23Z] nvidia: GPU 2: Xid 31: ChID 0x402a GPU page fault
[2026-03-15T02:10:24Z] kernel: oom_kill_process: kill process 18294 (runtime) score 987
[2026-03-15T02:10:25Z] runtime: failed to alloc 1.5GB for KV cache, returning OOM
```
Ben: autoscaler logs show it attempted scale ups but hit pool quota and maxReplicas limit at 60 for eu-west-1: 
```
2026-03-15T02:09:58Z autoscaler: desired_replicas=68 -> capped_to=60 (maxReplicas)
2026-03-15T02:10:05Z autoscaler: scale attempt failed: driver-registration-timeout on 3 nodes
```
Asha (oncall): so effective capacity lower than the physical GPU count because driver/node instability + autoscaler cap. That explains queue growth.
Samir: I'm marking 4 nodes as suspect (gpu-node-eu-8-{12,13,14,15}) — tainting and initiating drain: `kubectl taint nodes <node> gpu.unstable=true:NoSchedule`
Ben: doing that now, and removing them from the scheduler pool. Drain command: `kubectl drain gpu-node-eu-8-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`
Lena: routing change applied. Observability: queue dropping from 980 -> 560 after initial route shift. avg_wait_ms down to 2100. Still high.
Asha (oncall): customers impacted? Any high-traffic tenants hit hard?
Samir: tenant telemetry: 3 top customers seeing 30-70% increased latency and 502s start to appear when they hit GPU scheduling. Not full downtime but degraded.
Ben: I see repeated `Xid 31` and then `rm-init` driver re-loads. Drivers crash and node kubelet restarts, so those GPUs are offline for ~2-3m each.
Asha (oncall): temporary mitigations: 1) remove flapping nodes, 2) adjust autoscaler cap to allow higher headroom (if cloud quota allows), 3) model-fallback to smaller quantized variants for latency-sensitive customers. Anyone try a hot-restart of driver on node to see if it stabilizes?
Samir: attempted sudo modprobe nvidia; one node fails with `nvidia: probe failed with -22` — likely kernel-driver mismatch after recent kernel patch.
Lena: Check: kernel was rolled on 02/Mar to 5.15.24 -> some nodes got auto-updated last night. That lines up with when first Xid spikes started.
Ben: OK that matches. For now I recommend: keep nodes tainted/drained, spin up new nodes from the older kernel image (ami-gpu-stable-20260218) into pool-5/6 to recover capacity. Starting rollout now.
DeployBot: Launch request accepted: scaling group eu-west-1-standby -> +12 GPUs using ami-gpu-stable-20260218, estimated ready in 4m.
Asha (oncall): Good. Also reduce autoscaler cooldown to 30s to react faster once new nodes come up. Ben, can you keep watch on Xid errors in new nodes?
Ben: watching. I'll also push a post-deploy script to ensure drivers match kernel: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv,noheader` and compare against expected.
Samir: I've opened a short-lived routing fallback for flagged customers: forced to model-quantized-v2 (lower cost) for any scheduling failures to avoid 502s.
Asha (oncall): Customer comms: Ops to draft a status blurb — we should call this partial degradation (SLA not fully met for some tenants). Ben can you estimate ETA to recover to 95% capacity?
Ben: If new nodes come up without driver flaps, 8-10 minutes to bake and register, then autoscaler will rebalance. ETA ~12 minutes.
Lena: Queue length trending: 560 -> 320 now. avg_wait_ms -> 1100. Errors 502s dropping in last 3 min.
pagerduty-bot: Update: Incident IN-9923 escalated to P1 due to multiple enterprise tenants impacted.
Asha (oncall): Acknowledged. Escalation accepted. Assigning postmortem owner: Samir. Action items: (1) rollback last kernel rollout that caused instability OR pin GPU nodes to stable kernel images; (2) re-evaluate autoscaler maxReplicas setting and quota requests; (3) add early Xid detection to driver-monitoring; (4) customer RCA and timeline.
Samir: I accept postmortem. I'll coordinate with infra to rollback kernel and open cloud quota increase ticket if needed.
Ben: Monitoring: adding a temporary alert rule to fire at Xid rate > 5/min with dedicated slack paging.
Lena: Notifying support and account teams for top-3 affected customers with ETA ~12m and mitigation details.
Asha (oncall): Next oncall: @Ben will take the next 2h while I triage with infra leads. Ben, please update channel every 10m and mark when we reach steady state (queue < 100 and avg_wait_ms < 300).
Ben: Will do.
InfraBot: New nodes registered: 10/12 ready in eu-west-1 (ami-gpu-stable-20260218). GPUs registered: +40.
Lena: routing restored to 80% normal after autoscaler rebalanced. Queue now 78. avg_wait_ms 210.
Ben: All flapping nodes remain cordoned and tagged for kernel rollback. Observability shows Xid events have dropped to 0. We are at ~98% capacity.
Asha (oncall): Declaring mitigation successful. Continuing with follow-up: postmortem, kernel pin, autoscaler config change, and customer RCA. Closing pager duty in 30m unless regressions. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark: 
Samir: Filing follow-up tickets now and will draft timeline for postmortem.
Lena: I'll send the customer status update and link to this thread.
DeployBot: Pager update: Incident IN-9923: mitigated (status: partial restoration).
pagerduty-bot: Incident IN-9923 resolved by Asha (oncall).
